extracted.intended_audience: authors/distributors using the GNU Free Documentation License and TeX/LaTeX/ConTeXt users of the pgf/tikz graphics system
extracted.subtask_short: GNU FDL compliance and TikZ usage
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for copying, modifying, combining, translating, and distributing documents under the GNU Free Documentation License (including cover texts, invariant sections, History, Warranty Disclaimers, termination, and addendum) together with technical guidance for using the pgf/tikz system (input formats, backend drivers, output-format restrictions, design principles, and TikZ syntax).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirement to Preserve the Title
rubrics_metrics.description: A section 'Entitled XYZ' means a named subunit of the Document whose title either is precisely XYZ or contains XYZ in parentheses following text that translates XYZ in another language. To 'Preserve the Title' of such a section when you modify the Document means that it remains a section 'Entitled XYZ' according to this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying a Document, maintain section titles that are designated Entitled XYZ (including translations in parentheses) so they continue to meet this definition; this affects Preservation rules in section 4 and later modification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Warranty Disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Warranty Disclaimers next to the notice which states that this License applies to the Document are considered included by reference in this License, but only as regards disclaiming warranties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other implication that Warranty Disclaimers may have is void and has no effect on the meaning of this License; when preserving or copying, keep Warranty Disclaimers intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbatim Copying conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copy and distribute the Document in any medium, commercially or noncommercially, provided that this License, the copyright notices, and the license notice saying this License applies to the Document are reproduced in all copies, and that you add no other conditions whatsoever to those of this License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not use technical measures to obstruct or control reading or further copying (no DRM). You may accept compensation for copies. If distributing large numbers, additional conditions (see section 3) may apply. Lending and public display are permitted under the same conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying in Quantity (printed copies >100 and Opaque copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish printed copies (or media with printed covers) numbering more than 100 and the Document’s license notice requires Cover Texts, you must enclose the copies in covers that carry all required Cover Texts (Front-Cover Texts on front, Back-Cover Texts on back). Both covers must identify you as the publisher; the front cover must present the full title with all words equally prominent and visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may add other material on covers; cover-only changes preserving the title can be treated as verbatim copying. If required texts are too voluminous, put as many as fit on the cover and continue on adjacent pages. For Opaque copies >100, include a machine-readable Transparent copy with each Opaque copy or state a network location from which the public can download a complete Transparent copy; ensure the Transparent copy remains accessible until at least one year after the last distribution of that edition. It is requested (but not required) to contact the authors before redistributing many copies so they can supply an updated version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for Distributing Modiﬁed Versions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copy and distribute a Modified Version of the Document provided that you release the Modified Version under precisely this License and that the Modified Version fulfills a set of specific requirements (A–O) described in the License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Modified Version must be licensed identically and must itself permit further modification and distribution by subsequent possessors. The following detailed obligations (A–O) apply to title page, authorship, notices, invariant sections, History, Warranty Disclaimers, endorsements, and cover texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Distinct Title requirement (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use in the Title Page (and on the covers, if any) a title distinct from that of the Document and from those of previous versions (which should be listed in the History section). You may use the same title as a previous version only if the original publisher of that version gives permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Modified Version has a distinct title unless explicit permission is obtained from the original publisher; list previous versions in History when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Authorship listing requirement (B)
rubrics_metrics.description: List on the Title Page, as authors, one or more persons or entities responsible for authorship of the modifications in the Modified Version, together with at least five of the principal authors of the Document (all of its principal authors, if it has fewer than five), unless they release you from this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include modification authors plus the required number of original principal authors on the Title Page, unless you have releases from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Publisher statement on Title Page (C)
rubrics_metrics.description: State on the Title page the name of the publisher of the Modified Version, as the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Modified Version’s Title Page must explicitly name the publisher of that Modified Version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve and include copyright and license notices (D, E, F, H, G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve all the copyright notices of the Document; add an appropriate copyright notice for your modifications adjacent to the other copyright notices; include, immediately after the copyright notices, a license notice giving the public permission to use the Modified Version under the terms of this License (in the form shown in the Addendum); preserve in that license notice the full lists of Invariant Sections and required Cover Texts given in the Document’s license notice; include an unaltered copy of this License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain original copyright notices, add your own modification copyright, include the license notice and the complete lists of Invariant Sections/Cover Texts as they appear in the original, and include the unaltered license text inside the Modified Version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve and update History section (I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the section Entitled 'History', Preserve its Title, and add to it an item stating at least the title, year, new authors, and publisher of the Modified Version as given on the Title Page. If there is no section Entitled 'History' in the Document, create one stating the title, year, authors, and publisher of the Document as given on its Title Page, then add an item describing the Modified Version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure History contains an entry for the Modified Version and preserves prior history; if none existed, create the History section describing original Document and then add Modified Version entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve network locations for Transparent copies (J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the network location, if any, given in the Document for public access to a Transparent copy of the Document, and likewise the network locations given for previous versions it was based on. These may be placed in the 'History' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may omit a network location for a work that was published at least four years before the Document itself, or if the original publisher gives permission. Preserve network location entries when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve Acknowledgements and Dedications (K)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any section Entitled 'Acknowledgements' or 'Dedications', Preserve the Title of the section, and preserve in the section all the substance and tone of each of the contributor acknowledgements and/or dedications given therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter the substance or tone of these sections when creating Modified Versions; preserve their titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve Invariant Sections (L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve all the Invariant Sections of the Document, unaltered in their text and in their titles. Section numbers or the equivalent are not considered part of the section titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invariant Sections must remain exactly as in the original Document (text and title) in any Modified Version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Endorsements prohibition (M, N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete any section Entitled 'Endorsements'. Such a section may not be included in the Modified Version. Do not retitle any existing section to be Entitled 'Endorsements' or to conflict in title with any Invariant Section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All 'Endorsements' sections must be removed; do not create sections with that title or rename other sections to conflict with Invariant Section titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Preserve Warranty Disclaimers (O)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve any Warranty Disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any Warranty Disclaimers present in the original must be preserved in the Modified Version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Designating new front-matter as Invariant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Modified Version includes new front-matter sections or appendices that qualify as Secondary Sections and contain no material copied from the Document, you may optionally designate some or all of these sections as invariant by adding their titles to the list of Invariant Sections in the Modified Version’s license notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These added invariant titles must be distinct from any other section titles; only sections containing no copied material may be designated this way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Adding an 'Endorsements' section limited use
rubrics_metrics.description: You may add a section Entitled 'Endorsements', provided it contains nothing but endorsements of your Modified Version by various parties—for example, statements of peer review or that the text has been approved by an organization as the authoritative definition of a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an added 'Endorsements' section may only contain endorsements of the Modified Version itself and not other content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Limitations on adding Cover Texts
rubrics_metrics.description: You may add a passage of up to five words as a Front-Cover Text, and a passage of up to 25 words as a Back-Cover Text, to the end of the list of Cover Texts in the Modified Version. Only one passage of Front-Cover Text and one of Back-Cover Text may be added by (or through arrangements made by) any one entity. If the Document already includes a cover text for the same cover, previously added by you or by the same entity, you may not add another; but you may replace the old one on explicit permission from the previous publisher that added the old one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the per-entity limits and do not accumulate multiple cover-text additions for the same cover without permission; ensure added passages meet the word-count limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications: Use of original authors' and publishers' names
rubrics_metrics.description: The author(s) and publisher(s) of the Document do not by this License give permission to use their names for publicity for or to assert or imply endorsement of any Modified Version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use original authors' or publishers' names to imply endorsement or for publicity of the Modified Version without separate permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining Documents under the License
rubrics_metrics.description: You may combine the Document with other documents released under this License, provided that you include in the combination all of the Invariant Sections of all of the original documents, unmodified, and list them all as Invariant Sections of your combined work in its license notice, and that you preserve all their Warranty Disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined work need only contain one copy of this License; multiple identical Invariant Sections may be replaced with a single copy. If there are multiple Invariant Sections with the same name but different contents, make titles unique by adding the original author/publisher name or a unique number, and adjust the list in the license notice accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining: Merging History/Acknowledgements/Dedications and deleting Endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the combination, you must combine any sections Entitled 'History' in the various original documents, forming one section Entitled 'History'; likewise combine any sections Entitled 'Acknowledgements', and any sections Entitled 'Dedications'. You must delete all sections Entitled 'Endorsements'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When merging similarly titled sections, consolidate their contents into a single section; remove all Endorsements sections from the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of Documents rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may make a collection consisting of the Document and other documents released under this License, and replace the individual copies of this License in the various documents with a single copy included in the collection, provided that you follow the rules of this License for verbatim copying of each of the documents in all other respects.

rubrics_metrics.description: A compilation of the Document or its derivatives with other separate and independent documents or works is an 'aggregate' if the copyright resulting from the compilation is not used to limit the legal rights of the compilation’s users beyond what the individual works permit. When the Document is included in an aggregate, this License does not apply to the other works in the aggregate which are not themselves derivative works of the Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported TeX input formats for pgf/tikz
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf/tikz supports three major input formats: Donald Knuth’s plain TeX, Leslie Lamport’s LaTeX, and Hans Hagen’s ConTeXt. Commands differ slightly between formats (e.g., environment delimiters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX: use \usepackage{pgf} or \usepackage{tikz} (usually sufficient). Plain TeX: use \input{pgf.tex} or \input{tikz.tex} and replace \begin/\end environments with macro forms (\pgfpicture / \endpgfpicture); you may need to set \pgfsysdriver for some output formats. ConTeXt: use \usemodule[pgf] or \usemodule[tikz] and replace environment start/end with \start... / \stop... forms; you may need pgfmod to handle module-name-length limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the backend driver for pgf
rubrics_metrics.description: When TEX typesets your document it does not inherently know which program will process the .dvi or output; special commands differ between drivers. You must tell pgf which program/driver you intend to use, either through LaTeX graphics mechanisms or by redefining the macro \pgfsysdriver before loading pgf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set \pgfsysdriver to the appropriate driver file (e.g., pgfsys-dvips.def for dvips, pgfsys-pdftex.def for pdftex). In LaTeX this is usually automatic; for plain TeX or other configurations you may need to set it manually before loading pgf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing PDF output: driver capabilities and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf supports producing PDF via dvipdfm, pdftex (pdflatex), and vtex. The pgfsys-pdftex.def driver 'has the complete functionality'. Other drivers support most features but have restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pgfsys-dvipdfm.def: supports most features but (1) in LaTeX mode uses graphicx and does not support masking, (2) in plain TeX mode does not support image inclusion, (3) remembering of pictures (inter-picture connections) requires a recent pdftex running in DVI-mode. pgfsys-vtex.def: similar restrictions plus shading quality limitations, opacity unsupported, and remembering of pictures not supported. Alternatively, produce PDF by generating PostScript then converting to PDF (ps2pdf/Distiller) if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing PostScript output: driver capabilities and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The pgfsys-dvips.def driver (for (la)tex + dvips) and pgfsys-textures.def (for textures) include common PostScript support, but not all pgf features are equally supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common restrictions: (1) In LaTeX mode they use graphicx for graphics inclusion and do not support masking. (2) In plain TeX mode they do not support image inclusion. (3) shading is implemented but of lower quality than PDF driver. (4) opacity may only work with newer GhostScript. (5) remembering of pictures may require recent pdftex in DVI-mode. vtex can also produce PostScript with similar caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing HTML / SVG output (tex4ht) restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The tex4ht program (with pgfsys-tex4ht.def) can convert .dvi to .html and produce svg pictures for pgf graphics, but there are several limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions include: (1) In LaTeX mode it uses graphicx. (2) In plain TeX mode it does not support image inclusion. (3) remembering of pictures (inter-picture connections) not supported. (4) Text inside pgfpictures is poorly supported — only plain text without math/special chars and very simple math with subscripts/superscripts works reasonably well; variables are not properly italicized. Using special text (e.g., \alpha) may corrupt the graphic. (5) The bounding box truly crops the picture. (6) Matrices do not work. Recommendation: keep node text inside graphics very simple when targeting HTML/SVG via tex4ht.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing perfectly portable DVI output (pgfsys-dvi.def) limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The dvi driver can produce perfectly portable .dvi files by composing pictures entirely of black rectangles — the only primitive supported by TeX core — which severely limits capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is possible: text boxes, lines and curves (composed of many small rectangles), lines with differing widths, and transformations. What is not possible: filling, color, and advanced graphics. Use this driver only when output is very simple (e.g., only horizontal/vertical lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: TikZ design principles (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ frontend design goals: make an easy-to-learn and easy-to-use syntax for describing graphics, influenced by metafont (paths), pstricks (options), svg (styles), and others; includes features like meta-arrows and coordinate transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed basic design principles: 1) Special syntax for specifying points. 2) Special syntax for path specifications. 3) Actions on paths. 4) Key-value syntax for graphic parameters. 5) Special syntax for nodes. 6) Special syntax for trees. 7) Grouping of graphic parameters. 8) Coordinate transformation system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special syntax for specifying points (TikZ)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ provides multiple syntaxes for coordinates: (x unit,y unit) with units, polar coordinates (angle:radius), unitless coordinates in pgf's xy-coordinate system (e.g., (2,1)), three-number xyz coordinates (1,1,1), anchors of named shapes (first node.south), and relative coordinates with ++(x,y) or +(x,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ++(x,y) shifts the current point and updates it for subsequent relative commands; +(x,y) provides a relative point without changing the current point. Default unit vectors correspond to 1cm to the right/up unless reconfigured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special syntax for path specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Paths are specified as series of straight or curved segments using tokens like -- and cycle. Example triangular path: (5pt,0pt) -- (0pt,0pt) -- (0pt,5pt) -- cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paths need not be connected; path syntax is influenced by metapost and is the primary mechanism for describing shapes in TikZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions on paths (draw/fill/shade/clip and abbreviations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path can be drawn (stroking), filled, shaded, clipped, or any combination. Drawing uses a pen of given thickness; filling fills the interior and auto-closes a path prior to filling. Commands: \path[draw], \draw (abbrev), \fill (abbrev), \filldraw, \shade, \shadedraw, \clip etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands must be used inside {tikzpicture} environments. You can use different colors for fill and stroke. Use \draw[clip] or \path[draw,clip] for combining draw and clip; there is no separate \drawclip command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key-value syntax for graphic parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic rendering parameters (colors, dashing, clipping area, line width, etc.) are specified as key-value pairs passed as optional parameters to drawing and filling commands, e.g., \tikz \draw[line width=2pt,color=red] ... ;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The key-value mechanism (similar to pstricks) centralizes graphic options and enables styles and scoping to apply consistent parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special syntax for nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodes provide text or general elements in graphics; nodes are inserted at the current path position after the path has been rendered. Node options (e.g., node[circle,draw]{text}) can wrap text with shapes. Nodes can be named (name=(node name) or node[circle](name){text}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefined shapes include rectangle, circle, ellipse; custom shapes may be defined (more advanced). Node naming enables later reference by coordinates or anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special syntax for specifying trees
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ introduces a tree syntax integrated with nodes: a node can be followed by children introduced with the child keyword; children are nodes and can have nested children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trees inherit node options and can be altered via style settings (edge from parent, parent/child anchors, grow directions, etc.). The syntax makes it easy to declaratively specify hierarchical node structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of graphic parameters via scope environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use {scope} environments with optional graphic parameters to apply options to a block of drawing/filling commands; nested scopes or individual commands can override outer scope parameters. The {tikzpicture} environment behaves like a top-level scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group related commands for consistent styling; use scope nesting to override or limit effects; the optional argument to \begin{scope}[options] applies only within that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate transformation system and avoidance of canvas transforms
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ relies entirely on pgf’s coordinate transformation system for performing transformations; canvas transformations (a lower-level system) are not accessible from TikZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: canvas transforms must be used with care and often result in undesirable graphics (changing line widths, text wrong size); pgf also loses track of node/shape positions with canvas transforms. For details see referenced section (42.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical structure for TikZ files: package, environments, scopes, styles
rubrics_metrics.description: File structure: include the tikz package at top level; each graphic must be inside a {tikzpicture} environment; inside {tikzpicture} use {scope} environments to group commands; within scopes use \path commands to draw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic options can be given at any level (except package level) and apply to everything within that environment; use this hierarchy to manage styles and reuse parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading the package and libraries (practical rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Load TikZ via \usepackage{tikz} (LaTeX), \input tikz.tex (plain TeX), or \usemodule[tikz] / \usemodule[pgf] (ConTeXt). The package has no options and will load pgf and ancillary packages (e.g., xkeyval). Use \usetikzlibrary{...} to load additional libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pgf normally autodetects the correct driver, but when using plain TeX or ConTeXt with dvipdfm you must define \pgfsysdriver{pgfsys-dvipdfm.def} before inputting tikz.tex. Library lists are comma-separated; re-loading a library does nothing.
